summary: Iteration 19 validated all 4 new features shipped in this session (flight tracker, auto-refund on cancel, blackout calendar, tour upsell). Backend: 15/15 pytest passed in test_iteration19_flight_refund_blackout.py. Frontend: FlightTrackerCard on /taxi booking modal tested end-to-end — WU805 correctly returns Western Air GGT→NAS with populated arrival time, ZZ9999 shows flight-not-found, 'AB' does not fire a lookup (<3-char guard works), and the flight-pickup-aligned indicator renders when the current booking_date already matches the recommended pickup. TourUpsellCard was code-reviewed only (real Stripe session polling required to reach /payment-success — same limitation as iteration 18) but the underlying /api/tours endpoint returns >=2 active tours and the component wiring is correct.

minor.issue: When a booking is unpaid AND cancelled with >48h notice, cancellation_fee is set to 0.0 and refund_estimate is 0.0 (both because `paid` is false). The response body still exposes `eligible_for_refund: true` even though nothing was paid, which can be confusing. Not a bug per spec, but the semantics of 'eligible_for_refund' + fee=0 look inconsistent to a reader.

AviationStack free tier is HTTP-only (http://api.aviationstack.com) — cache mitigates but each cold flight number costs a call. Consider adding negative-response caching for unknown flight numbers (already implemented — cache stores the not-found result) and rate-limit per-IP.

action_items: OPTIONAL: normalise the cancel response so eligible_for_refund only reports true when a refund is actually issued (paid==true). Cosmetic — not blocking.
OPTIONAL: schedule a live Stripe test-session flow so /payment-success + TourUpsellCard get exercised by Playwright (currently only code-review verified).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1675 lines — well past the 700-line guideline. Extract flight tracker, blackout dates, and cancel/refund into feature routers alongside admin.py and payments.py.

_refresh_blackout_cache_sync() (server.py:216-231) is essentially a no-op when called from a running event loop — it just seeds an empty set and returns. The blackout check therefore relies on refresh_blackout_cache() being invoked by the admin endpoint. If the process is restarted while a blackout is set, the FIRST booking on that date will slip through until the admin endpoint is hit again. Fix: seed the cache on startup (add to configure()/lifespan) or move the check to `await db.site_config.find_one(...)` inline (single Mongo read).

lookup_flight has no per-IP rate limiting — a determined visitor could burn the 100-call/month AviationStack quota in seconds by cycling flight numbers. Add a simple sliding-window limiter or ban queries with >20 rpm from one IP.

cancel_booking exposes internal stripe/paypal error strings in refund_result.error verbatim (line 1147) — those can leak internal keys, request IDs, or infra hostnames. Sanitise before returning to public API.
AVIATIONSTACK_API_KEY is committed to /app/backend/.env in the repo (visible in this iteration) — rotate before pushing to a public branch.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Server clock in this environment is running at ~2026-07-29 (real time), so booking dates in tests must be > that. I use 2026-12-14 through 2026-12-21 for far-future scenarios. WU805 (Western Air GGT→NAS) is a REAL scheduled flight that AviationStack returns data for on any day of the month — do NOT change the test to a different flight number without checking AviationStack quota (100/mo). The FlightTrackerCard debounce is 750ms, so Playwright must wait >=3s after typing before asserting flight-info. To reach /payment-success in a browser test you'd need a Stripe Checkout live session — the polling loop /api/payments/status/{session_id} will 404 without one; alternatives are (a) add a test-only /api/dev/mock-paid-session endpoint or (b) drive the /pay/{booking_id} → Zelle mark-paid flow, but neither redirects to /payment-success.
